chapters.title: David Mourns Saul and Jonathan
chapters.html:
2 Samuel 1

The Amalekite's Report

1And it came to pass after the death of Saul, when David had returned from striking the Amalekites, that David stayed two days in Ziklag.

2And it came to pass on the third day that a man came from Saul's camp with his clothes torn and dirt on his head. When he came to David, he fell to the ground and paid homage.

3David said to him, "Where have you come from?" He said to him, "I have escaped from the camp of Israel."

4David said to him, "What happened? Tell me." He said, "The people fled from the battle, and many of the people also fell and died, and Saul and Jonathan his son are also dead."

5David said to the young man who was telling him, "How do you know that Saul and Jonathan his son are dead?"

6The young man who was telling him said, "I happened to be on Mount Gilboa, and there was Saul, leaning on his spear, and the chariots and the horsemen were closing in on him.

7He turned around and saw me, and called to me, and I said, 'Here I am.'

8He said to me, 'Who are you?' I said to him, 'I am an Amalekite.'

9He said to me, 'Stand over me and kill me, for agony has seized me, and yet my life is still whole in me.'

10So I stood over him and killed him, for I knew that he could not live after he had fallen. I took the crown that was on his head and the band that was on his arm, and I have brought them here to my lord."

11Then David took hold of his clothes and tore them, and so did all the men who were with him.

12They mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Saul and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of the LORD and for the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.

13David said to the young man who had told him, "Where are you from?" He said, "I am the son of a guest, an Amalekite."

14David said to him, "How were you not afraid to put out your hand to destroy the LORD's anointed?"

15Then David called one of the young men and said, "Go, strike him down." He struck him, and he died.

16David said to him, "Your blood is on your own head, for your own mouth has testified against you, saying, 'I have killed the LORD's anointed.'"

The Song of the Bow

17David sang this lament over Saul and over Jonathan his son,

18and he said it should be taught to the sons of Judah: The Bow. It is written in the Book of Jashar:

19"Your glory, O Israel, lies slain on your high places.
How the mighty have fallen!

20Tell it not in Gath,
proclaim it not in the streets of Ashkelon,
or the daughters of the Philistines will rejoice,
or the daughters of the uncircumcised will exult.

21Mountains of Gilboa,
let there be no dew or rain on you,
nor fields that yield offerings!
For there the shield of the mighty was defiled,
the shield of Saul, no longer anointed with oil.

22From the blood of the slain,
from the fat of the mighty,
the bow of Jonathan did not turn back,
and the sword of Saul did not return empty.

23Saul and Jonathan, beloved and lovely in their life,
and in their death they were not divided.
They were swifter than eagles,
they were stronger than lions.

24Daughters of Israel, weep over Saul,
who clothed you in scarlet and fine things,
who put ornaments of gold on your clothing.

25How the mighty have fallen
in the middle of the battle!
Jonathan lies slain on your high places.

26I am distressed for you, my brother Jonathan;
you were very dear to me.
Your love to me was wonderful,
more than the love of women.

27How the mighty have fallen,
and the weapons of war have perished!"

Notes

  • v1 "And it came to pass after the death of Saul" — the book opens as Joshua opens, after the death of Moses (Joshua 1:1), and Judges, after the death of Joshua (Judges 1:1). It continues 1 Samuel without a break.

  • vv6–10 "Saul, leaning on his spear… So I stood over him and killed him" — the account at Gilboa is different: Saul took the sword and fell on it, and his armor-bearer saw that he was dead (1 Samuel 31:4–5). There the archers found him; here it is chariots and horsemen. The Amalekite brings the crown and claims the death, and the claim kills him.

  • v9 "for agony has seized me" — ha-shavats, a word found only here in the Bible; its meaning is not certain. The Greek has a terrible darkness.

  • v13 "I am the son of a guest, an Amalekite" — ger, a foreigner living under Israel's protection and so under its law. He comes from the people David has just struck (v1; 1 Samuel 30:17), and the people Saul was sent to destroy (1 Samuel 15:3).

  • vv14, 16 "How were you not afraid to put out your hand to destroy the LORD's anointed?" — what David twice refused to do: who can put out his hand against the LORD's anointed and be guiltless? (1 Samuel 26:9; also 24:6). Your own mouth has testified against you: the man is judged by his own story.

  • v18 "The Bow… the Book of Jashar" — qeshet, bow, standing alone; the song is known by the weapon of Jonathan (v22). The Greek lacks the word. The Book of Jashar, sefer ha-yashar, the Book of the Upright, a lost collection of songs, is quoted also at Joshua 10:13.

  • vv19, 25 "Your glory, O Israel… on your high places" — ha-tsevi, which is also the gazelle, the swift animal of the hills. The line can be heard both ways. The Greek has Set up a pillar, O Israel.

  • v21 "the shield of Saul, no longer anointed with oil" — beli mashiach ba-shamen, without anointing with oil. A shield was oiled for battle, Rise up, you commanders, anoint the shield! (Isaiah 21:5); mashiach is also the word of the LORD's anointed (v14). The line holds both: the shield lies unoiled, and the anointed king is gone.

  • v23 "in their death they were not divided" — Jonathan chose David's cause (1 Samuel 20, 23:17) and died at his father's side (1 Samuel 31:2).

  • v26 "Your love to me was wonderful" — ahavatkha, the word of 1 Samuel 18:1–3, Jonathan loved him as his own soul. Nifle'atah, wonderful, from pele, what goes beyond the ordinary.

chapters.title: Two Kings
chapters.html:
2 Samuel 2

David King in Hebron

1And it came to pass after this that David inquired of the LORD, "Shall I go up into one of the towns of Judah?" The LORD said to him, "Go up." David said, "Where shall I go up?" He said, "To Hebron."

2So David went up there, with his two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel.

3David brought up the men who were with him, each with his household, and they settled in the towns of Hebron.

4Then the men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah. They told David, "It was the men of Jabesh-gilead who buried Saul."

5David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-gilead and said to them, "Blessed are you by the LORD, because you showed this loyal love to your lord Saul and buried him.

6Now may the LORD show loyal love and faithfulness to you. I too will do you good because you have done this.

7Now then, let your hands be strong, and be men of valor, for your lord Saul is dead, and the house of Judah has anointed me king over them."

Ish-bosheth King over Israel

8But Abner son of Ner, the commander of Saul's army, took Ish-bosheth son of Saul and brought him over to Mahanaim.

9He made him king over Gilead, the Ashurites and Jezreel, over Ephraim and Benjamin, and over all Israel.

10Ish-bosheth son of Saul was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and he reigned two years. But the house of Judah followed David.

11The time that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.

The Pool of Gibeon

12Abner son of Ner and the servants of Ish-bosheth son of Saul went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.

13Joab son of Zeruiah and the servants of David also went out, and they met them at the pool of Gibeon. They sat down, the one side on one side of the pool and the other on the other side of the pool.

14Abner said to Joab, "Let the young men arise and fight a contest before us." Joab said, "Let them arise."

15So they arose and went over by number: twelve for Benjamin and for Ish-bosheth son of Saul, and twelve of the servants of David.

16Each caught his opponent by the head and thrust his sword into his opponent's side, and they fell down together. So that place was called Helkath-hazzurim, which is in Gibeon.

17The battle was very hard that day, and Abner and the men of Israel were beaten before the servants of David.

Asahel

18The three sons of Zeruiah were there, Joab, Abishai and Asahel. Asahel was as swift of foot as a gazelle in the field.

19Asahel pursued Abner, and he did not turn to the right or to the left from following Abner.

20Abner looked behind him and said, "Is that you, Asahel?" He said, "It is."

21Abner said to him, "Turn aside to your right or to your left, seize one of the young men and take his gear for yourself." But Asahel would not turn aside from following him.

22Abner said again to Asahel, "Turn aside from following me. Why should I strike you to the ground? How then could I lift up my face to Joab your brother?"

23But he refused to turn aside. So Abner struck him in the belly with the butt of his spear, and the spear came out at his back. He fell there and died on the spot. All who came to the place where Asahel had fallen and died stood still.

24But Joab and Abishai pursued Abner. As the sun was going down, they came to the hill of Ammah, which lies before Giah on the way to the wilderness of Gibeon.

25The sons of Benjamin gathered behind Abner and became one band, and they took their stand on the top of a hill.

26Then Abner called to Joab, "Shall the sword devour forever? Do you not know that the end will be bitter? How long will it be before you tell the people to turn back from pursuing their brothers?"

27Joab said, "As God lives, if you had not spoken, the people would have gone on pursuing their brothers until morning."

28So Joab blew the horn, and all the people stopped. They no longer pursued Israel, and they fought no more.

29Abner and his men went all that night through the Arabah. They crossed the Jordan, went through the whole Bithron, and came to Mahanaim.

30Joab came back from pursuing Abner and gathered all the people. Of David's servants nineteen men were missing, besides Asahel.

31But the servants of David had struck down of Benjamin and of Abner's men three hundred and sixty men, who died.

32They took up Asahel and buried him in his father's tomb at Bethlehem. Joab and his men marched all night, and day broke on them at Hebron.

Notes

  • v1 "David inquired of the LORD… To Hebron" — as he did before every move in the wilderness (1 Samuel 23:2, 30:8). Hebron was the town of Abraham's burial place (Genesis 23:19) and the portion of Caleb (Joshua 14:13), in the heart of Judah.

  • vv4–7 "the men of Jabesh-gilead who buried Saul… this loyal love" — chesed. David's first act as king is to thank the town that honored Saul (1 Samuel 31:11–13), and to let it know that Judah now has a king.

  • vv8–10 "Ish-bosheth son of Saul" — Ish-boshet, man of shame. 1 Chronicles names Saul's son Eshbaal, man of Baal (1 Chronicles 8:33, 9:39). The Hebrew of Samuel has boshet, shame, in the place of the name Baal, as it has Jerubbesheth for Jerubbaal (11:21). The Greek has Iebosthe.

  • v10 "he reigned two years… seven years and six months" — the two reigns do not match in length. The text gives both figures and does not reconcile them.

  • vv14–16 "Let the young men arise and fight a contest" — vi-sachaqu, let them play, the word for sport and entertainment. The contest ends with all twenty-four dead. Helkath-hazzurim is the field of flints or of blades; the Greek has the Portion of the Plotters.

  • v18 "as swift of foot as a gazelle in the field" — tsevi, the word of David's lament, Your glory, or gazelle, O Israel (1:19).

  • vv21–23 "Why should I strike you to the ground?… the butt of his spear" — Abner tries twice to turn Asahel away and does not want the blood feud with Joab that comes of it (3:27). He kills him with the back end of the spear, not the point. Ha-chomesh, the belly, is where Joab strikes Abner in return (3:27).

  • v26 "Shall the sword devour forever?" — la-netsach, forever. Abner calls the men of Judah their brothers: the war is between tribes of one people.

  • v29 "the whole Bithron" — ha-bitron, from batar, to cut in two: a ravine or cleft, or a region so named. What exactly it was is not known.

chapters.title: The Death of Abner
chapters.html:
2 Samuel 3

Sons Born in Hebron

1The war between the house of Saul and the house of David was long. David grew stronger and stronger, while the house of Saul grew weaker and weaker.

2Sons were born to David in Hebron. His firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam of Jezreel;

3his second, Chileab, by Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel; the third, Absalom son of Maacah, daughter of Talmai king of Geshur;

4the fourth, Adonijah son of Haggith; the fifth, Shephatiah son of Abital;

5and the sixth, Ithream, by Eglah, David's wife. These were born to David in Hebron.

Abner Turns to David

6And it came to pass, while there was war between the house of Saul and the house of David, that Abner was making himself strong in the house of Saul.

7Saul had had a concubine whose name was Rizpah, daughter of Aiah. Ish-bosheth said to Abner, "Why have you gone in to my father's concubine?"

8Abner was very angry at the words of Ish-bosheth and said, "Am I a dog's head of Judah? This day I keep showing loyal love to the house of Saul your father, to his brothers and to his friends, and I have not handed you over into the hand of David, and yet today you charge me with a fault concerning a woman.

9May God do so to Abner, and more also, if I do not do for David what the LORD has sworn to him,

10to transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul and set up the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan to Beersheba."

11Ish-bosheth could not answer Abner another word, because he was afraid of him.

12Abner sent messengers to David on his own behalf, saying, "Whose is the land? Make your covenant with me, and my hand will be with you to bring all Israel over to you."

13He said, "Good. I will make a covenant with you. But one thing I ask of you: you shall not see my face unless you first bring Michal, Saul's daughter, when you come to see my face."

14Then David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth son of Saul, saying, "Give me my wife Michal, whom I betrothed to myself for a hundred foreskins of the Philistines."

15So Ish-bosheth sent and took her from her husband, from Paltiel son of Laish.

16Her husband went with her, weeping as he walked behind her all the way to Bahurim. Then Abner said to him, "Go back." So he went back.

17Abner had a word with the elders of Israel, saying, "For some time you have been seeking David as king over you.

18Now then, do it, for the LORD has spoken of David, saying, 'By the hand of My servant David I will save My people Israel from the hand of the Philistines and from the hand of all their enemies.'"

19Abner also spoke in the hearing of Benjamin. Then Abner went to speak in the hearing of David at Hebron all that seemed good to Israel and to the whole house of Benjamin.

20When Abner came to David at Hebron with twenty men, David made a feast for Abner and the men who were with him.

21Abner said to David, "Let me arise and go and gather all Israel to my lord the king, so that they may make a covenant with you, and you may reign over all that your soul desires." So David sent Abner away, and he went in peace.

Joab Kills Abner

22Just then the servants of David and Joab came from a raid, bringing much spoil with them. But Abner was not with David in Hebron, for he had sent him away, and he had gone in peace.

23When Joab and all the army that was with him came, Joab was told, "Abner son of Ner came to the king, and he sent him away, and he has gone in peace."

24Joab came to the king and said, "What have you done? Abner came to you. Why is it that you have sent him away, and he is gone?

25You know Abner son of Ner, that he came to deceive you, to learn your going out and your coming in, and to learn all that you are doing."

26When Joab came out from David, he sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from the cistern of Sirah. But David did not know.

27When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside into the middle of the gate to speak with him quietly, and there he struck him in the belly, and he died, for the blood of Asahel his brother.

28Afterward, when David heard of it, he said, "I and my kingdom are guiltless before the LORD forever of the blood of Abner son of Ner.

29May it fall on the head of Joab and on all his father's house, and may the house of Joab never be without one who has a discharge, or one with blight, or one who holds a spindle, or one who falls by the sword, or one who lacks bread!"

30So Joab and Abishai his brother killed Abner, because he had put their brother Asahel to death at Gibeon in the battle.

David Mourns Abner

31Then David said to Joab and to all the people who were with him, "Tear your clothes, put on sackcloth and mourn before Abner." King David walked behind the bier.

32They buried Abner in Hebron, and the king lifted up his voice and wept at Abner's grave, and all the people wept.

33The king sang a lament for Abner and said,
"Should Abner die as a fool dies?

34Your hands were not bound,
your feet were not put in fetters.
As one falls before the wicked,
you have fallen."
Then all the people wept over him again.

35Then all the people came to make David eat bread while it was still day, but David swore, "May God do so to me, and more also, if I taste bread or anything else before the sun goes down."

36All the people took notice, and it pleased them, as everything the king did pleased all the people.

37So all the people and all Israel understood that day that it had not been the king's will to put Abner son of Ner to death.

38The king said to his servants, "Do you not know that a prince and a great man has fallen this day in Israel?

39Today I am weak, though anointed king, and these men, the sons of Zeruiah, are too hard for me. May the LORD repay the one who does evil according to his evil!"

Notes

  • v1 "David grew stronger and stronger, while the house of Saul grew weaker and weaker" — holekh ve-chazeq… holekhim ve-dallim, going and growing strong… going and growing weak: the same Hebrew pattern as the boy Samuel kept growing (1 Samuel 2:26).

  • vv2–5 "Sons were born to David in Hebron" — the list names the sons whose stories fill the rest of the book: Amnon (chapter 13), Absalom (chapters 13–18), Adonijah (1 Kings 1). Absalom's mother is the daughter of the king of Geshur, the land to which Absalom will flee (13:37).

  • v7 "Why have you gone in to my father's concubine?" — to take a dead king's woman was to lay claim to his place. Absalom does it openly with David's concubines (16:21–22), and Adonijah's request for Abishag costs him his life (1 Kings 2:22–25).

  • v8 "Am I a dog's head of Judah?" — the insult David used of himself before Saul, a dead dog (1 Samuel 24:14). Of Judah stings because Abner has been fighting Judah for Saul's house. The Greek lacks of Judah.

  • vv9–10, 18 "what the LORD has sworn to David… By the hand of My servant David I will save My people" — the book has not told of an oath or saying in these words. Abner speaks as if the LORD's choice of David were known to all Israel (1 Samuel 15:28, 16:13, 23:17, 24:20).

  • vv13–16 "you shall not see my face unless you first bring Michal… weeping as he walked behind her" — the wife given as a bride-price of foreskins (1 Samuel 18:25–27) and given away by Saul (1 Samuel 25:44). David's claim to her is a claim on Saul's house.

  • v27 "he struck him in the belly… for the blood of Asahel his brother" — el ha-chomesh, where Abner struck Asahel (2:23). Joab kills him in the middle of the gate, where the elders sat to judge (Deuteronomy 21:19), without judgment.

  • v29 "one who has a discharge, or one with blight, or one who holds a spindle" — zav, the discharge of Leviticus 15:2; metsora, one with blight; machaziq ba-pelekh, one who holds a spindle, the tool of a woman at work (Proverbs 31:19): a man unfit for war. Some read pelekh as crutch; the spindle is the other place the word stands.

  • vv33–34 "Should Abner die as a fool dies?" — ha-kemot naval, as Nabal dies, or as a fool dies; the word is the name of Abigail's husband (1 Samuel 25:25). Abner, who was free, with hands not bound, died by treachery, not as a criminal or a fool.

  • v39 "Today I am weak, though anointed king… the sons of Zeruiah are too hard for me" — rakh, soft, tender. David can mourn Abner but cannot punish Joab. The debt is paid at the end of David's life, when he charges Solomon about Joab (1 Kings 2:5–6).

his second, Chileab, by Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel; the third, Absalom son of Maacah, daughter of Talmai king of Geshur;
the fourth, Adonijah son of Haggith; the fifth, Shephatiah son of Abital;
and the sixth, Ithream, by Eglah, David's wife. These were born to David in Hebron.
Abner Turns to David
And it came to pass, while there was war between the house of Saul and the house of David, that Abner was making himself strong in the house of Saul.
Saul had had a concubine whose name was Rizpah, daughter of Aiah. Ish-bosheth said to Abner, "Why have you gone in to my father's concubine?"

Abner was very angry at the words of Ish-bosheth and said, "Am I a dog's head of Judah? This day I keep showing loyal love to the house of Saul your father, to his brothers and to his friends, and I have not handed you over into the hand of David, and yet today you charge me with a fault concerning a woman.
May God do so to Abner, and more also, if I do not do for David what the LORD has sworn to him,
to transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul and set up the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan to Beersheba."
Ish-bosheth could not answer Abner another word, because he was afraid of him.
Abner sent messengers to David on his own behalf, saying, "Whose is the land? Make your covenant with me, and my hand will be with you to bring all Israel over to you."
He said, "Good. I will make a covenant with you. But one thing I ask of you: you shall not see my face unless you first bring Michal, Saul's daughter, when you come to see my face."
Then David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth son of Saul, saying, "Give me my wife Michal, whom I betrothed to myself for a hundred foreskins of the Philistines."
So Ish-bosheth sent and took her from her husband, from Paltiel son of Laish.
Her husband went with her, weeping as he walked behind her all the way to Bahurim. Then Abner said to him, "Go back." So he went back.
Abner had a word with the elders of Israel, saying, "For some time you have been seeking David as king over you.
Now then, do it, for the LORD has spoken of David, saying, 'By the hand of My servant David I will save My people Israel from the hand of the Philistines and from the hand of all their enemies.'"
Abner also spoke in the hearing of Benjamin. Then Abner went to speak in the hearing of David at Hebron all that seemed good to Israel and to the whole house of Benjamin.
When Abner came to David at Hebron with twenty men, David made a feast for Abner and the men who were with him.

Abner said to David, "Let me arise and go and gather all Israel to my lord the king, so that they may make a covenant with you, and you may reign over all that your soul desires." So David sent Abner away, and he went in peace.
Joab Kills Abner
Just then the servants of David and Joab came from a raid, bringing much spoil with them. But Abner was not with David in Hebron, for he had sent him away, and he had gone in peace.
When Joab and all the army that was with him came, Joab was told, "Abner son of Ner came to the king, and he sent him away, and he has gone in peace."
Joab came to the king and said, "What have you done? Abner came to you. Why is it that you have sent him away, and he is gone?
You know Abner son of Ner, that he came to deceive you, to learn your going out and your coming in, and to learn all that you are doing."
When Joab came out from David, he sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from the cistern of Sirah. But David did not know.
When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside into the middle of the gate to speak with him quietly, and there he struck him in the belly, and he died, for the blood of Asahel his brother.
Afterward, when David heard of it, he said, "I and my kingdom are guiltless before the LORD forever of the blood of Abner son of Ner.

May it fall on the head of Joab and on all his father's house, and may the house of Joab never be without one who has a discharge, or one with blight, or one who holds a spindle, or one who falls by the sword, or one who lacks bread!"

The king sang a lament for Abner and said, "Should Abner die as a fool dies?
Your hands were not bound, your feet were not put in fetters. As one falls before the wicked, you have fallen." Then all the people wept over him again.
Then all the people came to make David eat bread while it was still day, but David swore, "May God do so to me, and more also, if I taste bread or anything else before the sun goes down."
All the people took notice, and it pleased them, as everything the king did pleased all the people.
So all the people and all Israel understood that day that it had not been the king's will to put Abner son of Ner to death.
The king said to his servants, "Do you not know that a prince and a great man has fallen this day in Israel?
Today I am weak, though anointed king, and these men, the sons of Zeruiah, are too hard for me. May the LORD repay the one who does evil according to his evil!"

chapters.title: The Murder of Ish-bosheth
chapters.html:
2 Samuel 4

Rechab and Baanah

1When Saul's son heard that Abner had died in Hebron, his hands went limp, and all Israel was dismayed.

2Saul's son had two men who were captains of raiding bands. The name of the one was Baanah and the name of the other Rechab, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, of the sons of Benjamin, for Beeroth also is counted as part of Benjamin.

3The Beerothites had fled to Gittaim, and they have lived there as guests to this day.

4Jonathan, Saul's son, had a son who was lame in his feet. He was five years old when the news about Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel. His nurse picked him up and fled, and as she hurried to flee, he fell and became lame. His name was Mephibosheth.

5Rechab and Baanah, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, set out and came in the heat of the day to the house of Ish-bosheth, as he was taking his midday rest.

6They came into the middle of the house as if to fetch wheat, and they struck him in the belly. Then Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.

7They came into the house as he lay on his bed in his bedroom, and they struck him and killed him and cut off his head. They took his head and went by the way of the Arabah all night.

8They brought the head of Ish-bosheth to David at Hebron and said to the king, "Here is the head of Ish-bosheth son of Saul, your enemy, who sought your life. The LORD has given my lord the king vengeance this day on Saul and on his seed."

David's Judgment

9David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, "As the LORD lives, who has redeemed my life out of every distress,

10when the one who told me, 'Saul is dead,' thought he was bringing good news, I seized him and killed him at Ziklag, which was the reward I gave him for his news.

11How much more, when wicked men have killed a righteous man in his own house on his bed! And now shall I not require his blood from your hand and wipe you from the earth?"

12David commanded the young men, and they killed them, cut off their hands and their feet and hung them up beside the pool at Hebron. But they took the head of Ish-bosheth and buried it in the tomb of Abner at Hebron.

Notes

  • v1 "his hands went limp" — va-yirpu yadav. With Abner dead, Saul's son has lost the man who made him king (2:8). The Hebrew calls him only Saul's son here and in v2; the Greek names him Mephibosheth, as it does throughout this chapter.

  • vv2–3 "sons of Rimmon the Beerothite… they have lived there as guests" — garim, the fixed word for guests. Beeroth was one of the towns of the Gibeonites who made a treaty with Joshua (Joshua 9:17). The murderers are Benjaminites, of Saul's own tribe.

  • v4 "Jonathan… had a son who was lame in his feet… Mephibosheth" — the verse stands in the middle of the murder story: with Ish-bosheth dead, the only grandson of Saul left of Jonathan's line is a lame child. He returns in chapter 9, when David seeks one of Saul's house for Jonathan's sake (9:1–3). His name is Merib-baal in 1 Chronicles 8:34; Samuel again has boshet, shame, for Baal, as with Ish-bosheth (2:8).

  • vv6–7 "They came into the middle of the house as if to fetch wheat… They came into the house as he lay on his bed" — the Hebrew tells the entry and the killing twice. The Greek of v6 is different: the doorkeeper of the house was cleaning wheat, and she dozed and slept, and Rechab and Baanah slipped in.

  • v8 "The LORD has given my lord the king vengeance this day on Saul and on his seed" — the murderers speak as if the LORD had done their work. David has refused to put out his hand against the LORD's anointed (1 Samuel 26:9) and sworn not to cut off Saul's seed (1 Samuel 24:21–22).

  • vv9–10 "who has redeemed my life out of every distress… I seized him and killed him at Ziklag" — David takes an oath by the LORD who delivered him, and judges the murderers by the case of the Amalekite (1:14–16).

  • v11 "a righteous man in his own house on his bed" — ish tsaddiq: Ish-bosheth did no wrong to the men who killed him. Wipe you from the earth, u-vi'arti, the verb of the law's refrain, so you shall purge the evil from among you (Deuteronomy 17:7).

  • v12 "cut off their hands and their feet and hung them up beside the pool at Hebron" — the sentence is carried out openly, at the pool of the town. The tomb of Abner: Saul's son is buried with Saul's commander at Hebron.

chapters.title: David King over All Israel
chapters.html:
2 Samuel 5

The Anointing at Hebron

1All the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and said, "We are your bone and your flesh.

2In times past, when Saul was king over us, it was you who led Israel out and brought them in. The LORD said to you, 'You shall shepherd My people Israel, and you shall be leader over Israel.'"

3So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and King David made a covenant with them at Hebron before the LORD, and they anointed David king over Israel.

4David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.

5At Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.

Jerusalem

6The king and his men went to Jerusalem against the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land. They said to David, "You will not come in here; even the blind and the lame will turn you away," meaning, "David cannot come in here."

7But David took the stronghold of Zion, that is, the City of David.

8David said on that day, "Whoever would strike the Jebusites, let him get up the water shaft to reach the lame and the blind, who are hated by David's soul." That is why they say, "The blind and the lame shall not come into the house."

9David lived in the stronghold and called it the City of David. David built the city all around from the Millo inward.

10David grew greater and greater, and the LORD, the God of hosts, was with him.

11Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, with cedar wood, carpenters and stonemasons, and they built David a house.

12David knew that the LORD had established him as king over Israel, and that He had exalted his kingdom for the sake of His people Israel.

13David took more concubines and wives from Jerusalem after he came from Hebron, and more sons and daughters were born to David.

14These are the names of those born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan and Solomon,

15Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg and Japhia,

16Elishama, Eliada and Eliphelet.

Victories over the Philistines

17When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over Israel, all the Philistines went up to seek David. David heard of it and went down to the stronghold.

18The Philistines had come and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.

19David inquired of the LORD, "Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will You give them into my hand?" The LORD said to David, "Go up, for I will certainly give the Philistines into your hand."

20David came to Baal-perazim, and David struck them there. He said, "The LORD has broken through my enemies before me like a breakthrough of waters." So he called the name of that place Baal-perazim.

21The Philistines left their idols there, and David and his men carried them away.

22The Philistines came up yet again and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.

23When David inquired of the LORD, He said, "You shall not go up. Go around behind them and come against them opposite the balsam trees.

24And it shall come to pass, when you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, that you shall act quickly, for then the LORD will have gone out before you to strike the army of the Philistines."

25David did as the LORD commanded him, and he struck down the Philistines from Geba all the way to Gezer.

Notes

  • v1 "We are your bone and your flesh" — the words of kinship, as Laban said to Jacob, Surely you are my bone and my flesh (Genesis 29:14). The tribes that fought for Saul's house now claim David as their own.

  • v2 "You shall shepherd My people Israel" — tir'eh, the shepherd's word; David was taken from tending the sheep (1 Samuel 16:11). Leader, nagid, the word the LORD used of Saul (1 Samuel 9:16) and then of the man after His own heart (1 Samuel 13:14).

  • v3 "a covenant with them… before the LORD" — the king binds himself to the elders, and they anoint him. This is David's third anointing: by Samuel among his brothers (1 Samuel 16:13), by Judah at Hebron (2:4), and now by all Israel.

  • vv6–8 "even the blind and the lame will turn you away… the water shaft" — the Jebusites boast that their walls need only the blind and the lame to defend them. David turns their taunt back: his men are to get up the water shaft, ba-tsinnor, and strike the lame and the blind. Tsinnor occurs elsewhere only in Psalm 42:7, at the sound of your waterfalls; its sense here is uncertain. The saying at the end became a proverb, The blind and the lame shall not come into the house. The Greek has let him touch with the dagger.

  • v10 "David grew greater and greater" — holekh ve-gadol, the pattern of 3:1, David grew stronger and stronger, and of the boy Samuel (1 Samuel 2:26).

  • v13 "David took more concubines and wives" — the law of the king: He shall not multiply wives for himself, so that his heart does not turn aside (Deuteronomy 17:17). The list of sons includes Solomon.

  • v20 "Baal-perazim… like a breakthrough of waters" — Ba'al Peratsim, Lord of breakthroughs, from parats, to break through, as a flood breaks a dam. The same verb names the next place of the ark's story, Perez-uzzah, when the LORD had broken out against Uzzah (6:8).

  • v21 "The Philistines left their idols there, and David and his men carried them away" — the reverse of the day the Philistines carried off the ark of God (1 Samuel 4:11). Chronicles adds that David ordered them burned (1 Chronicles 14:12), as the law commands (Deuteronomy 7:25).

  • vv23–24 "the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees" — ha-bekha'im, trees named only here and in the parallel in Chronicles (1 Chronicles 14:14–15); balsam is one guess among several. The Greek has the place of weeping. The sound is the LORD's army going out ahead of David.

chapters.title: The Ark Brought to Jerusalem
chapters.html:
2 Samuel 6

Uzzah

1David again gathered all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.

2David arose and went with all the people who were with him from Baale-judah to bring up from there the ark of God, which is called by the name, the name of the LORD of hosts, who is enthroned on the cherubim above it.

3They set the ark of God on a new cart and carried it from the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill. Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, were driving the new cart.

4They carried it from the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill, with the ark of God, and Ahio was walking in front of the ark.

5David and all the house of Israel were celebrating before the LORD with all their might and with songs, with lyres, harps, tambourines, rattles and cymbals.

6When they came to the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah put out his hand to the ark of God and took hold of it, for the oxen stumbled.

7The anger of the LORD burned against Uzzah, and God struck him down there for his error, and he died there beside the ark of God.

8David was angry because the LORD had broken out against Uzzah, and that place is called Perez-uzzah to this day.

9David was afraid of the LORD that day and said, "How can the ark of the LORD come to me?"

10So David was not willing to take the ark of the LORD into the City of David to be with him. David turned it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.

11The ark of the LORD stayed in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite three months, and the LORD blessed Obed-edom and all his household.

David Dances

12King David was told, "The LORD has blessed the house of Obed-edom and all that belongs to him because of the ark of God." So David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-edom to the City of David with rejoicing.

13When those who carried the ark of the LORD had gone six steps, he sacrificed an ox and a fatted calf.

14David danced with all his might before the LORD, and David was wearing a linen ephod.

15So David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD with shouting and with the sound of the horn.

16As the ark of the LORD came into the City of David, Michal the daughter of Saul looked down through the window and saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD, and she despised him in her heart.

17They brought in the ark of the LORD and set it in its place inside the tent that David had pitched for it. Then David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.

18When David had finished offering the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of hosts.

19He distributed to all the people, the whole multitude of Israel, both men and women, to each a loaf of bread, a portion of meat and a cake of raisins. Then all the people went away, each to his house.

Michal

20David returned to bless his household, and Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David and said, "How the king of Israel has honored himself today, uncovering himself today in the sight of his servants' slave girls, as one of the empty fellows shamelessly uncovers himself!"

21David said to Michal, "It was before the LORD, who chose me above your father and above all his house to appoint me leader over the people of the LORD, over Israel. I will celebrate before the LORD.

22I will make myself even more lightly esteemed than this, and I will be humble in my own eyes. But by the slave girls you have spoken of, by them I shall be held in honor."

23Michal the daughter of Saul had no child to the day of her death.

Notes

  • v2 "from Baale-judah… called by the name, the name of the LORD of hosts" — Ba'alei Yehudah, the town Joshua calls Baalah, that is, Kiriath-jearim (Joshua 15:9), where the ark had stayed since the Philistines returned it (1 Samuel 7:1–2). The name, the name stands twice in the Hebrew.

  • vv3–4 "carried it from the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill" — the words stand twice in the Hebrew, at the end of v3 and the start of v4; the Greek has them once. The text keeps the Hebrew as it is. A new cart: the Philistines sent the ark home on a new cart (1 Samuel 6:7). The law gives the ark to the Levites to carry on poles (Numbers 4:15, Exodus 25:14); David's first attempt copies the Philistines.

  • v5 "with all their might and with songs" — the Hebrew has with all kinds of cypress wood, be-khol atsei veroshim. The Greek and the parallel in Chronicles have with all their might and with songs, be-khol oz u-ve-shirim (1 Chronicles 13:8); the Hebrew letters of the two readings are close. The text follows the Greek and Chronicles.

  • vv6–7 "Uzzah put out his hand… God struck him down there for his error" — al ha-shal, a word found only here; error or irreverence is the sense from the context. Chronicles has because he put out his hand on the ark (1 Chronicles 13:10). The law warned that the Kohathites they shall not touch the holy things, or they will die (Numbers 4:15).

  • v8 "Perez-uzzah… the LORD had broken out against Uzzah" — perets, the word of Baal-perazim, where the LORD broke through David's enemies (5:20). The same power that broke out for David now breaks out at his carelessness.

  • v11 "the LORD blessed Obed-edom and all his household" — a Gittite, a man of Gath, keeps the ark that killed Uzzah, and is blessed by it.

  • v14 "David danced with all his might… wearing a linen ephod" — ephod bad, the garment of the boy Samuel serving at Shiloh (1 Samuel 2:18) and of the priests of Nob (1 Samuel 22:18). Mekharker, whirling, a verb found only in this chapter.

  • v16 "Michal the daughter of Saul… despised him in her heart" — she is called the daughter of Saul three times here (vv16, 20, 23) and never David's wife. She once loved David (1 Samuel 18:20) and let him down through a window to save his life (1 Samuel 19:12); now she looks down through a window and despises him.

  • v19 "a portion of meat and a cake of raisins" — eshpar, found only here and in the parallel (1 Chronicles 16:3); its meaning is uncertain, and a portion of meat is one reading of it.

  • vv21–23 "who chose me above your father… Michal had no child" — David answers the daughter of Saul with the LORD's choice of him over Saul's house. With Michal childless, no heir of Saul's line comes from David's house.

As the ark of the LORD came into the City of David, Michal the daughter of Saul looked down through the window and saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD, and she despised him in her heart.
They brought in the ark of the LORD and set it in its place inside the tent that David had pitched for it. Then David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.
When David had finished offering the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of hosts.

He distributed to all the people, the whole multitude of Israel, both men and women, to each a loaf of bread, a portion of meat and a cake of raisins. Then all the people went away, each to his house.
Michal

David returned to bless his household, and Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David and said, "How the king of Israel has honored himself today, uncovering himself today in the sight of his servants' slave girls, as one of the empty fellows shamelessly uncovers himself!"
David said to Michal, "It was before the LORD, who chose me above your father and above all his house to appoint me leader over the people of the LORD, over Israel. I will celebrate before the LORD.
I will make myself even more lightly esteemed than this, and I will be humble in my own eyes. But by the slave girls you have spoken of, by them I shall be held in honor."
Michal the daughter of Saul had no child to the day of her death.

chapters.title: The LORD's Covenant with David
chapters.html:
2 Samuel 7

"Will You Build Me a House?"

1And it came to pass, when the king lived in his house and the LORD had given him rest from all his enemies around him,

2that the king said to Nathan the prophet, "See now, I live in a house of cedar, but the ark of God stays inside curtains."

3Nathan said to the king, "Go, do all that is in your heart, for the LORD is with you."

4And it came to pass that same night that the word of the LORD came to Nathan:

5"Go and tell My servant David, 'Thus says the LORD: Will you build Me a house to dwell in?

6I have not lived in a house from the day I brought the sons of Israel up from Egypt to this day, but I have been moving about in a tent for My dwelling.

7Wherever I have moved about among all the sons of Israel, did I ever speak a word to one of the tribes of Israel whom I commanded to shepherd My people Israel, saying, "Why have you not built Me a house of cedar?"'

The Promise

8Now then, say this to My servant David: 'Thus says the LORD of hosts: I took you from the pasture, from following the sheep, to be leader over My people, over Israel.

9I have been with you wherever you went and have cut off all your enemies before you. I will make you a great name, like the name of the great ones on the earth.

10I will appoint a place for My people Israel and will plant them, so that they may dwell in their own place and be disturbed no more. The wicked shall afflict them no more as at first,

11from the day I commanded judges over My people Israel. I will give you rest from all your enemies. The LORD declares to you that the LORD will make you a house.

12When your days are fulfilled and you lie down with your fathers, I will raise up your seed after you, who shall come from your body, and I will establish his kingdom.

13He shall build a house for My name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.

14I will be his father, and he shall be My son. When he does wrong, I will discipline him with the rod of men and with the blows of the sons of men.

15But My loyal love shall not depart from him, as I took it from Saul, whom I put away from before you.

16Your house and your kingdom shall be made sure forever before you; your throne shall be established forever.'"

17In accordance with all these words and all this vision, so Nathan spoke to David.

David's Prayer

18Then King David went in and sat before the LORD and said, "Who am I, O Lord GOD, and what is my house, that You have brought me this far?

19Yet this was too small in Your eyes, O Lord GOD; You have spoken also of Your servant's house for a long time to come. And this is the instruction for mankind, O Lord GOD!

20What more can David say to You? For You know Your servant, O Lord GOD.

21For the sake of Your word and according to Your own heart, You have done all this greatness, to make Your servant know it.

22Therefore You are great, O Lord GOD, for there is none like You, and there is no God besides You, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

23Who is like Your people, like Israel, the one nation on earth whom God went to redeem as a people for Himself, to make a name for Himself, and to do for you great and awesome things for Your land, before Your people whom You redeemed for Yourself from Egypt, from nations and their gods?

24You established for Yourself Your people Israel to be Your people forever, and You, O LORD, became their God.

25And now, O LORD God, confirm forever the word You have spoken concerning Your servant and concerning his house, and do as You have spoken.

26May Your name be great forever, saying, 'The LORD of hosts is God over Israel,' and may the house of Your servant David be established before You.

27For You, O LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, have made it known to Your servant, saying, 'I will build you a house.' That is why Your servant has found courage to pray this prayer to You.

28And now, O Lord GOD, You are God, and Your words are true, and You have promised this good thing to Your servant.

29And now, may it please You to bless the house of Your servant, so that it may continue forever before You. For You, O Lord GOD, have spoken, and with Your blessing let the house of Your servant be blessed forever."

Notes

  • vv1–2 "the LORD had given him rest… the ark of God stays inside curtains" — the rest the law promised, He gives you rest from all your enemies around you (Deuteronomy 12:10), after which the LORD would choose a place for His name (Deuteronomy 12:11). The king's cedar house stands beside the ark's tent of yeri'ah, curtains.

  • v5 "Will you build Me a house to dwell in?" — a question in the Hebrew. Chronicles and the Greek make it a statement, You shall not build Me a house (1 Chronicles 17:4).

  • vv5, 11, 13, 16 "a house" — bayit is house, temple and dynasty. David wants to build the LORD a house; the LORD answers that the LORD will make you a house. David's son will build the house of stone (v13), and David's house, his line, will be made sure (v16).

  • v8 "I took you from the pasture, from following the sheep" — the youngest son who was tending the sheep when Samuel came (1 Samuel 16:11).

  • v10 "I will plant them" — the promise of the Song at the Sea: You will bring Your people in and plant them on the mountain of Your inheritance (Exodus 15:17).

  • v14 "I will be his father, and he shall be My son" — the letter to the Hebrews applies the words to Jesus: I will be a Father to Him, and He shall be a Son to Me (Hebrews 1:5). In Samuel the next words are when he does wrong, I will discipline him: the son is first of all David's heir.

  • v15 "But My loyal love shall not depart from him, as I took it from Saul" — chesed, the covenant loyalty the LORD keeps. Saul lost the kingdom; the promise to David's line does not depend on the son's goodness.

  • v16 "Your house and your kingdom shall be made sure forever" — ne'eman, the word Abigail used first, the LORD will surely make my lord a sure house (1 Samuel 25:28), and the promise once made of a faithful priest (1 Samuel 2:35).

  • v18 "Who am I, O Lord GOD, and what is my house?" — David's words before Saul, Who am I… that I should be son-in-law to the king? (1 Samuel 18:18). Adonai YHWH, Lord GOD, seven times in the prayer.

  • vv19, 23 "this is the instruction for mankind… from nations and their gods" — torat ha-adam, a phrase whose sense here is not certain; Chronicles has a different reading, You have regarded me as a man of high rank (1 Chronicles 17:17). In v23 the Hebrew is also hard: Chronicles has by driving out nations (1 Chronicles 17:21). The text stays with the Hebrew in both.

chapters.title: David's Victories
chapters.html:
2 Samuel 8

The Wars

1And it came to pass after this that David struck the Philistines and subdued them, and David took Metheg-ammah out of the hand of the Philistines.

2He struck Moab and measured them with a line, making them lie down on the ground. He measured two lines to put to death and one full line to keep alive. The Moabites became David's servants and brought tribute.

3David also struck Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to restore his power at the river Euphrates.

4David captured from him a thousand chariots, seven thousand horsemen and twenty thousand foot soldiers. David hamstrung all the chariot horses, but left enough of them for a hundred chariots.

5When the Arameans of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck twenty-two thousand men of the Arameans.

6Then David put garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and the Arameans became David's servants and brought tribute. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.

7David took the shields of gold that were on the servants of Hadadezer and brought them to Jerusalem.

8From Betah and from Berothai, towns of Hadadezer, King David took a great quantity of bronze.

9When Toi king of Hamath heard that David had struck the whole army of Hadadezer,

10Toi sent Joram his son to King David to greet him and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer and struck him, for Hadadezer had been at war with Toi. Joram brought with him articles of silver, of gold and of bronze.

11These also King David dedicated to the LORD, together with the silver and gold he had dedicated from all the nations he had subdued:

12from Aram, from Moab, from the sons of Ammon, from the Philistines and from Amalek, and from the spoil of Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah.

13David made a name for himself when he returned from striking down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.

14He put garrisons in Edom; throughout all Edom he put garrisons, and all the Edomites became David's servants. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.

David's Officials

15So David reigned over all Israel, and David did justice and righteousness for all his people.

16Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder;

17Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar were priests; Seraiah was secretary;

18Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and David's sons were priests.

Notes

  • v1 "David took Metheg-ammah" — meteg ha-ammah, the bridle of the forearm, or of the mother city: a place name or a figure for control of the Philistine capital. Chronicles has he took Gath and its villages (1 Chronicles 18:1).

  • v2 "He measured two lines to put to death and one full line to keep alive" — the Moabites are laid on the ground and measured off by rope. David had once sent his parents to the king of Moab for safety (1 Samuel 22:3–4); the text does not say what changed.

  • v4 "a thousand chariots, seven thousand horsemen" — the Hebrew has a thousand seven hundred horsemen and no chariots, though the same verse speaks of all the chariot horses and a hundred chariots. The Greek and Chronicles have a thousand chariots, seven thousand horsemen (1 Chronicles 18:4). The text follows them.

  • v4 "David hamstrung all the chariot horses" — va-ye'aqqer, as the LORD told Joshua, You shall hamstring their horses and burn their chariots (Joshua 11:6).

  • vv6, 14 "The LORD gave David victory wherever he went" — va-yosha, saved. The line is said twice, after the wars in the north and in the south.

  • vv7–8 "the shields of gold… a great quantity of bronze" — the Greek adds that Shishak king of Egypt later took the gold shields, and that Solomon made the bronze sea, pillars and vessels from the bronze. Chronicles has the second addition (1 Chronicles 18:8). The text stays with the Hebrew.

  • v13 "eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt" — the Hebrew has Aram; the Greek has Edom, and so does Chronicles, Abishai… struck Edom in the Valley of Salt, eighteen thousand (1 Chronicles 18:12). The next verse is about garrisons in Edom. Aram and Edom differ in Hebrew by one letter. The text follows the Greek and Chronicles.

  • v15 "David did justice and righteousness for all his people" — mishpat u-tsedaqah, what the LORD chose Abraham to teach his house, they shall keep the way of the LORD, to do righteousness and judgment (Genesis 18:19).

  • v17 "Ahimelech son of Abiathar" — in 1 Samuel it is the other way round: Abiathar son of Ahimelech escaped from Nob (1 Samuel 22:20). The Hebrew and the Greek both have it as it stands here.

  • v18 "and David's sons were priests" — kohanim. Chronicles has David's sons were the chief officers at the king's side (1 Chronicles 18:17), and the Greek has court officials. The Hebrew word is the ordinary word for priest; the text keeps it.

chapters.title: David and Mephibosheth
chapters.html:
2 Samuel 9

"Is There Anyone Left of the House of Saul?"

1David said, "Is there still anyone left of the house of Saul, so that I may show him loyal love for Jonathan's sake?"

2There was a servant of the house of Saul whose name was Ziba, and they called him to David. The king said to him, "Are you Ziba?" He said, "Your servant."

3The king said, "Is there no one left of the house of Saul, so that I may show him the loyal love of God?" Ziba said to the king, "There is still a son of Jonathan, who is lame in his feet."

4The king said to him, "Where is he?" Ziba said to the king, "He is in the house of Machir son of Ammiel, in Lo-debar."

5So King David sent and brought him from the house of Machir son of Ammiel, from Lo-debar.

6Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, son of Saul, came to David and fell on his face and paid homage. David said, "Mephibosheth!" He said, "Here is your servant."

7David said to him, "Do not be afraid, for I will surely show you loyal love for the sake of Jonathan your father. I will restore to you all the land of Saul your grandfather, and you shall eat bread at my table always."

8He paid homage and said, "What is your servant, that you should look on a dead dog like me?"

At the King's Table

9Then the king called Ziba, Saul's servant, and said to him, "All that belonged to Saul and to all his house I have given to your master's grandson.

10You and your sons and your servants shall work the land for him and bring in the produce, so that your master's grandson may have bread to eat. But Mephibosheth, your master's grandson, shall always eat bread at my table." Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.

11Ziba said to the king, "According to all that my lord the king commands his servant, so your servant will do." So Mephibosheth ate at David's table like one of the king's sons.

12Mephibosheth had a young son whose name was Mica. All who lived in Ziba's house were Mephibosheth's servants.

13So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, for he always ate at the king's table. He was lame in both his feet.

Notes

  • vv1, 3, 7 "loyal love for Jonathan's sake… the loyal love of God" — chesed, the covenant word of David and Jonathan: Do not cut off your loyal love from my house forever (1 Samuel 20:15). The loyal love of God is the phrase Jonathan used, the loyal love of the LORD (1 Samuel 20:14).

  • v3 "lame in his feet" — the fall from his nurse's arms when the news of Gilboa came (4:4).

  • v4 "in Lo-debar" — Lo Devar, no word or no thing, a town east of the Jordan. Machir son of Ammiel of Lo-debar will later bring supplies to David when he flees from Absalom (17:27–29).

  • v6 "Mephibosheth!… Here is your servant" — hinneh avdekha, Here is your servant, the answer of one ready to serve, as Samuel answered Here I am (1 Samuel 3:4).

  • v7 "Do not be afraid" — the grandson of the king David replaced has reason to fear. David had sworn to Saul not to cut off his seed (1 Samuel 24:21–22), and now gives his grandson Saul's land and a place at his table.

  • v8 "that you should look on a dead dog like me?" — the words David used of himself before Saul, After a dead dog! (1 Samuel 24:14). The grandson of Saul now uses them before David.

  • v10 "Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants" — the man who works the land holds the larger house. When David flees from Absalom, Ziba will speak against his master and be given all that belonged to him (16:1–4).

  • v11 "So Mephibosheth ate at David's table" — the Hebrew has at my table, as if David were speaking, though the sentence stands after Ziba's words. The Greek has at David's table, and vv7, 10 and 13 all speak of the king's table. The text follows the Greek.

  • v13 "He was lame in both his feet" — the chapter ends as it began (v3). He eats at the king's table and cannot run from it.

chapters.title: The War with Ammon and Aram
chapters.html:
2 Samuel 10

David's Envoys Shamed

1And it came to pass after this that the king of the sons of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his place.

2David said, "I will show loyal love to Hanun son of Nahash, as his father showed loyal love to me." So David sent his servants to comfort him concerning his father, and David's servants came to the land of the sons of Ammon.

3But the princes of the sons of Ammon said to Hanun their lord, "Do you think David is honoring your father because he has sent comforters to you? Has David not sent his servants to you to search out the city, to spy it out and to overthrow it?"

4So Hanun took David's servants, shaved off half of each one's beard, cut their garments in half as far as their buttocks, and sent them away.

5When David was told, he sent to meet them, for the men were deeply humiliated. The king said, "Stay in Jericho until your beards grow, and then come back."

Joab and Abishai

6When the sons of Ammon saw that they had become a stench to David, the sons of Ammon sent and hired the Arameans of Beth-rehob and the Arameans of Zobah, twenty thousand foot soldiers, the king of Maacah with a thousand men, and the men of Tob, twelve thousand men.

7When David heard it, he sent Joab and all the army, the mighty men.

8The sons of Ammon came out and drew up for battle at the entrance of the gate, while the Arameans of Zobah and Rehob and the men of Tob and Maacah were by themselves in the open country.

9When Joab saw that the battle was set against him in front and behind, he chose some of all the chosen men of Israel and drew them up against the Arameans.

10The rest of the people he put in the hand of Abishai his brother, and he drew them up against the sons of Ammon.

11He said, "If the Arameans are too strong for me, then you shall help me. But if the sons of Ammon are too strong for you, then I will come to help you.

12Be strong, and let us show ourselves strong for our people and for the cities of our God. The LORD will do what is good in His eyes."

13So Joab and the people who were with him drew near to battle against the Arameans, and they fled before him.

14When the sons of Ammon saw that the Arameans had fled, they fled before Abishai and went into the city. Then Joab turned back from the sons of Ammon and came to Jerusalem.

The Battle at Helam

15When the Arameans saw that they had been struck down before Israel, they gathered together.

16Hadadezer sent and brought out the Arameans who were beyond the River, and they came to Helam, with Shobach the commander of Hadadezer's army at their head.

17When David was told, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan and came to Helam. The Arameans drew up against David and fought with him.

18The Arameans fled before Israel, and David killed of the Arameans the men of seven hundred chariots and forty thousand horsemen. He struck Shobach the commander of their army, and he died there.

19When all the kings who were servants of Hadadezer saw that they had been struck down before Israel, they made peace with Israel and served them. So the Arameans were afraid to help the sons of Ammon any more.

Notes

  • v2 "as his father showed loyal love to me" — chesed. His father is Nahash the Ammonite, who besieged Jabesh-gilead and demanded every right eye (1 Samuel 11:1–2). The text does not say what loyal love Nahash showed David.

  • v3 "to search out the city, to spy it out and to overthrow it" — u-le-hofkhah, to overturn it, the word used of Sodom and Gomorrah, He overturned those cities (Genesis 19:25). The princes read comfort as reconnaissance.

  • v4 "shaved off half of each one's beard, cut their garments in half as far as their buttocks" — shetoteihem, from shet, as in with buttocks uncovered, the nakedness of Egypt (Isaiah 20:4). The half-shaving and the cut robes are public shame; the men cannot go home as they are.

  • v5 "Stay in Jericho" — the first town on the road west across the Jordan. David keeps them out of sight until the shame is gone.

  • v6 "they had become a stench to David" — niv'ashu, the word of Israel has also become a stench to the Philistines (1 Samuel 13:4).

  • v6 "the king of Maacah" — the Greek has the king of Amalek, here and in v8. Chronicles has the king of Maacah and his people (1 Chronicles 19:7), and Maacah lies with Zobah and Rehob in the north. The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • v6 "the men of Tob" — ish tov, the land where Jephthah fled and gathered his band (Judges 11:3).

  • v12 "Be strong… The LORD will do what is good in His eyes" — chazaq, what Moses said to Joshua, Be strong and courageous (Deuteronomy 31:7). The last line is Eli's, Let Him do what is good in His eyes (1 Samuel 3:18).

speech.text: 2 Samuel 10
David's Envoys Shamed
And it came to pass after this that the king of the sons of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his place.

David said, "I will show loyal love to Hanun son of Nahash, as his father showed loyal love to me." So David sent his servants to comfort him concerning his father, and David's servants came to the land of the sons of Ammon.

But the princes of the sons of Ammon said to Hanun their lord, "Do you think David is honoring your father because he has sent comforters to you? Has David not sent his servants to you to search out the city, to spy it out and to overthrow it?"
So Hanun took David's servants, shaved off half of each one's beard, cut their garments in half as far as their buttocks, and sent them away.
When David was told, he sent to meet them, for the men were deeply humiliated. The king said, "Stay in Jericho until your beards grow, and then come back."
Joab and Abishai

When the sons of Ammon saw that they had become a stench to David, the sons of Ammon sent and hired the Arameans of Beth-rehob and the Arameans of Zobah, twenty thousand foot soldiers, the king of Maacah with a thousand men, and the men of Tob, twelve thousand men.
When David heard it, he sent Joab and all the army, the mighty men.
The sons of Ammon came out and drew up for battle at the entrance of the gate, while the Arameans of Zobah and Rehob and the men of Tob and Maacah were by themselves in the open country.
When Joab saw that the battle was set against him in front and behind, he chose some of all the chosen men of Israel and drew them up against the Arameans.
The rest of the people he put in the hand of Abishai his brother, and he drew them up against the sons of Ammon.
He said, "If the Arameans are too strong for me, then you shall help me. But if the sons of Ammon are too strong for you, then I will come to help you.
Be strong, and let us show ourselves strong for our people and for the cities of our God. The LORD will do what is good in His eyes."
So Joab and the people who were with him drew near to battle against the Arameans, and they fled before him.
When the sons of Ammon saw that the Arameans had fled, they fled before Abishai and went into the city. Then Joab turned back from the sons of Ammon and came to Jerusalem.
The Battle at Helam
When the Arameans saw that they had been struck down before Israel, they gathered together.
Hadadezer sent and brought out the Arameans who were beyond the River, and they came to Helam, with Shobach the commander of Hadadezer's army at their head.
When David was told, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan and came to Helam. The Arameans drew up against David and fought with him.
The Arameans fled before Israel, and David killed of the Arameans the men of seven hundred chariots and forty thousand horsemen. He struck Shobach the commander of their army, and he died there.

When all the kings who were servants of Hadadezer saw that they had been struck down before Israel, they made peace with Israel and served them. So the Arameans were afraid to help the sons of Ammon any more.

chapters.title: David and Bathsheba
chapters.html:
2 Samuel 11

The Roof of the King's House

1And it came to pass at the turn of the year, at the time when kings go out, that David sent Joab, and his servants with him, and all Israel. They destroyed the sons of Ammon and besieged Rabbah. But David stayed in Jerusalem.

2And it came to pass one evening that David got up from his bed and walked about on the roof of the king's house, and from the roof he saw a woman bathing. The woman was very beautiful to look at.

3David sent and inquired about the woman, and someone said, "Is this not Bathsheba daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?"

4So David sent messengers and took her. She came to him, and he lay with her; she had been purifying herself from her uncleanness. Then she returned to her house.

5The woman conceived, and she sent and told David, "I am pregnant."

Uriah

6Then David sent word to Joab: "Send me Uriah the Hittite." So Joab sent Uriah to David.

7When Uriah came to him, David asked about the welfare of Joab, the welfare of the people and the welfare of the war.

8David said to Uriah, "Go down to your house and wash your feet." Uriah went out of the king's house, and a gift from the king followed him.

9But Uriah slept at the entrance of the king's house with all the servants of his lord, and he did not go down to his house.

10They told David, "Uriah did not go down to his house." David said to Uriah, "Have you not just come from a journey? Why did you not go down to your house?"

11Uriah said to David, "The ark and Israel and Judah are staying in booths, and my lord Joab and the servants of my lord are camped in the open field. Shall I then go to my house to eat and to drink and to lie with my wife? As you live, and as your soul lives, I will not do this thing."

12David said to Uriah, "Stay here today also, and tomorrow I will send you off." So Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day and the next.

13David invited him, and he ate and drank in his presence, and David made him drunk. In the evening he went out to lie on his bed with the servants of his lord, but he did not go down to his house.

The Letter to Joab

14And it came to pass in the morning that David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it by the hand of Uriah.

15In the letter he wrote, "Put Uriah in front, where the fighting is fiercest, then draw back from him, so that he is struck down and dies."

16And it came to pass, as Joab kept watch on the city, that he put Uriah at the place where he knew there were men of valor.

17The men of the city came out and fought with Joab, and some of the people, of David's servants, fell. Uriah the Hittite also died.

18Then Joab sent and told David all the news of the battle.

19He instructed the messenger, "When you have finished telling the king all the news of the battle,

20if the king's anger rises and he says to you, 'Why did you go so near the city to fight? Did you not know that they would shoot from the wall?

21Who struck down Abimelech son of Jerubbesheth? Was it not a woman who threw an upper millstone on him from the wall, so that he died at Thebez? Why did you go so near the wall?' then you shall say, 'Your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead too.'"

22So the messenger went, and he came and told David all that Joab had sent him to say.

23The messenger said to David, "The men were stronger than we were and came out against us into the field, but we drove them back to the entrance of the gate.

24Then the archers shot at your servants from the wall, and some of the king's servants died. Your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead too."

25David said to the messenger, "Say this to Joab: 'Do not let this thing be evil in your eyes, for the sword devours now one and now another. Press your attack on the city and overthrow it.' So encourage him."

In David's House

26When Uriah's wife heard that Uriah her husband was dead, she mourned for her husband.

27When the mourning was over, David sent and gathered her into his house, and she became his wife and bore him a son. But the thing that David had done was evil in the eyes of the LORD.

Notes

  • v1 "at the time when kings go out… But David stayed in Jerusalem" — the Hebrew letters spell ha-mal'akhim, the messengers, but the aleph carries a mark (rafe) telling the reader not to sound it; without it the word is kings. The Greek has kings, and so does Chronicles, at the time when kings go out (1 Chronicles 20:1). The text follows them. The king whose time it is to go out sends others and stays home.

  • v2 "on the roof of the king's house" — on this same roof Absalom will pitch a tent and go in to his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel (16:22), as Nathan will say, before this sun (12:11–12).

  • v3 "Bathsheba daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite" — Eliam son of Ahithophel the Gilonite (23:34) and Uriah the Hittite (23:39) are both named among David's mighty men. The Greek has Eliab; Chronicles calls her Bath-shua daughter of Ammiel (1 Chronicles 3:5).

  • v4 "she had been purifying herself from her uncleanness" — mitqaddeshet mi-tum'atah: the purification after her monthly separation (Leviticus 15:19, 28). It places the conception after that separation, so the child of v5 is David's.

  • v7 "the welfare of Joab, the welfare of the people and the welfare of the war" — shalom three times. David asks after the peace of a war he has left to others.

  • v8 "wash your feet… a gift from the king" — go home for the night; Uriah's answer in v11 shows what he understood. Mas'at, the word for the portions Joseph sent from his table (Genesis 43:34).

  • v11 "The ark and Israel and Judah are staying in booths… As you live, and as your soul lives" — sukkot. David told Ahimelech that women have indeed been kept from us, as always when I set out (1 Samuel 21:5); Uriah keeps that rule in Jerusalem. He swears by David's own life.

  • v14 "sent it by the hand of Uriah" — Uriah carries the letter that orders his death.

  • v21 "Abimelech son of Jerubbesheth… an upper millstone… at Thebez" — Gideon was called Jerubbaal (Judges 6:32); besheth, shame, stands for baal here, as in Ish-bosheth and Mephibosheth. The death is told in Judges 9:50–53. The Greek adds to v22 that David was angry with Joab, and gives David the whole speech Joab had predicted. The text stays with the Hebrew.

  • vv25, 27 "Do not let this thing be evil in your eyes… evil in the eyes of the LORD" — al yera be-einekha et ha-davar ha-zeh and va-yera ha-davar… be-einei YHWH. David tells Joab not to let the thing be evil in his eyes; the chapter ends by saying it was evil in the LORD's.
