chapters.title: Nathan and David
chapters.html:
2 Samuel 12

The Poor Man's Ewe Lamb

1The LORD sent Nathan to David. He came to him and said to him, "There were two men in one city, one rich and the other poor.

2The rich man had very many flocks and herds,

3but the poor man had nothing except one little ewe lamb, which he had bought. He raised it, and it grew up with him and with his children. It would eat from his morsel and drink from his cup and lie in his bosom, and it was like a daughter to him.

4A traveler came to the rich man, and he could not bear to take from his own flock or his own herd to prepare for the wayfarer who had come to him. So he took the poor man's ewe lamb and prepared it for the man who had come to him."

5David's anger burned hot against the man, and he said to Nathan, "As the LORD lives, the man who has done this deserves to die!

6He shall repay the ewe lamb fourfold, because he did this thing and because he had no pity."

"You Are the Man"

7Nathan said to David, "You are the man! Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: 'I anointed you king over Israel, and I delivered you from the hand of Saul.

8I gave you your master's house and your master's wives into your bosom, and I gave you the house of Israel and of Judah. If that had been too little, I would have added to you as much again and as much again.

9Why have you despised the word of the LORD, to do what is evil in My eyes? Uriah the Hittite you have struck down with the sword, and his wife you have taken to be your wife; him you have killed with the sword of the sons of Ammon.

10Now therefore the sword shall never depart from your house, because you have despised Me and have taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your wife.'

11Thus says the LORD: 'I am about to raise up evil against you out of your own house. I will take your wives before your eyes and give them to your neighbor, and he shall lie with your wives before the eyes of this sun.

12For you did it in secret, but I will do this thing before all Israel and before the sun.'"

13David said to Nathan, "I have sinned against the LORD." Nathan said to David, "The LORD also has put away your sin; you shall not die.

14However, because by this deed you have utterly scorned the enemies of the LORD, the son who is born to you shall surely die."

The Child Dies

15Then Nathan went to his house. The LORD struck the child that Uriah's wife had borne to David, and he became very sick.

16David sought God for the boy. David fasted, and he went in and lay all night on the ground.

17The elders of his house stood beside him to raise him from the ground, but he would not, and he did not eat bread with them.

18And it came to pass on the seventh day that the child died. David's servants were afraid to tell him that the child was dead, for they said, "While the child was still alive, we spoke to him, and he would not listen to our voice. How can we say to him, 'The child is dead'? He may do something terrible."

19When David saw that his servants were whispering together, David understood that the child was dead. David said to his servants, "Is the child dead?" They said, "He is dead."

20Then David got up from the ground, washed, anointed himself and changed his clothes. He went into the house of the LORD and worshiped. Then he went to his own house, and when he asked, they set bread before him, and he ate.

21His servants said to him, "What is this thing you have done? While the child was alive, you fasted and wept, but when the child died, you got up and ate bread."

22He said, "While the child was still alive, I fasted and wept, for I said, 'Who knows? The LORD may be gracious to me, and the child may live.'

23But now he is dead. Why should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I will go to him, but he will not return to me."

Solomon

24David comforted Bathsheba his wife, and he went in to her and lay with her. She bore a son, and she called his name Solomon. The LORD loved him

25and sent word by the hand of Nathan the prophet, and he called his name Jedidiah, because of the LORD.

The Capture of Rabbah

26Joab fought against Rabbah of the sons of Ammon and captured the royal city.

27Joab sent messengers to David and said, "I have fought against Rabbah; I have also captured the city of waters.

28So now gather the rest of the people, camp against the city and capture it, or I will capture the city myself, and it will be called by my name."

29So David gathered all the people and went to Rabbah, fought against it and captured it.

30He took the crown of their king from his head. Its weight was a talent of gold, with a precious stone, and it was placed on David's head. He brought out the spoil of the city, a very great amount.

31He brought out the people who were in it and set them to the saws and the iron picks and the iron axes, and made them pass through the brick kiln. So he did to all the cities of the sons of Ammon. Then David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.

Notes

  • v3 "lie in his bosom, and it was like a daughter to him" — ke-vat; bat, daughter, is the first part of Bathsheba's name. In his bosom returns in v8: the LORD gave David his master's wives into your bosom.

  • vv5–7 "deserves to die… fourfold… You are the man!" — ben mavet, what Saul said of David, he deserves to die (1 Samuel 20:31). Fourfold is the law's payment for a stolen sheep, four sheep in place of the sheep (Exodus 22:1); the Greek has sevenfold. The text keeps the Hebrew. Attah ha-ish: David has passed sentence on himself.

  • v9 "to do what is evil in My eyes" — the written text has in his eyes; the text follows the read form, in My eyes. It answers 11:27, the thing that David had done was evil in the eyes of the LORD. With the sword of the sons of Ammon: David killed Uriah by another's hand.

  • v10 "the sword shall never depart from your house" — three of David's sons will die by violence: Amnon (13:28–29), Absalom (18:14–15) and Adonijah (1 Kings 2:25).

  • vv11–12 "before the eyes of this sun… you did it in secret" — the threat is fulfilled on the roof where it began, when Absalom goes in to his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel (16:22).

  • v13 "I have sinned against the LORD… you shall not die" — chatati la-YHWH. Saul said I have sinned twice and asked to be honored before the elders (1 Samuel 15:24, 30); David says it once and asks for nothing. Psalm 51 is headed when Nathan the prophet came to him, after he had gone in to Bathsheba. You shall not die lifts the sentence David pronounced in v5.

  • v14 "you have utterly scorned the enemies of the LORD" — the sense is that David has scorned the LORD (v10, you have despised Me). The enemies of turns the words away from God, as in May God do so to the enemies of David (1 Samuel 25:22). The Greek has the same wording.

  • vv24–25 "she called his name Solomon… Jedidiah, because of the LORD" — the written text has he called; the text follows the read form, she called. Shelomoh is from the root of shalom. Yedidyah, beloved of the LORD, follows The LORD loved him.

  • v30 "the crown of their king" — malkam, which is also the name of the god of the Ammonites, Milcom the loathsome thing of the Ammonites (1 Kings 11:5). The Greek has both, Melchol their king.

  • v31 "set them to the saws and the iron picks and the iron axes… the brick kiln" — va-yasem ba-megerah, put them at the saw, the verb used for setting people to work. Chronicles has va-yasar (1 Chronicles 20:3), one letter different, a verb whose meaning there is unclear. The written text has malken; the text follows the read form, malben, brick kiln or brick mold.

chapters.title: Amnon and Tamar
chapters.html:
2 Samuel 13

Amnon and Tamar

1And it came to pass after this that Absalom son of David had a beautiful sister whose name was Tamar, and Amnon son of David loved her.

2Amnon was so distressed over Tamar his sister that he made himself sick, for she was a virgin, and it seemed impossible to Amnon to do anything to her.

3Amnon had a friend whose name was Jonadab son of Shimeah, David's brother, and Jonadab was a very wise man.

4He said to him, "Why are you so haggard, son of the king, morning after morning? Will you not tell me?" Amnon said to him, "I love Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister."

5Jonadab said to him, "Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick. When your father comes to see you, say to him, 'Please let my sister Tamar come and give me bread to eat. Let her prepare the food in my sight, so that I may see it and eat from her hand.'"

6So Amnon lay down and pretended to be sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said to the king, "Please let my sister Tamar come and make a couple of heart-cakes in my sight, so that I may eat from her hand."

7Then David sent word to Tamar at the house: "Go now to your brother Amnon's house and prepare food for him."

8So Tamar went to her brother Amnon's house, where he was lying down. She took dough, kneaded it, made the heart-cakes in his sight and baked them.

9Then she took the pan and set them out before him, but he refused to eat. Amnon said, "Send everyone out from me." So everyone went out from him.

10Then Amnon said to Tamar, "Bring the food into the inner room, so that I may eat from your hand." Tamar took the heart-cakes she had made and brought them to Amnon her brother in the inner room.

11When she brought them near to him to eat, he took hold of her and said to her, "Come, lie with me, my sister."

12She said to him, "No, my brother! Do not violate me, for such a thing is not done in Israel. Do not do this outrage.

13As for me, where could I carry my disgrace? You would be like one of the fools in Israel. Now please speak to the king, for he will not keep me from you."

14But he would not listen to her voice. He overpowered her, violated her and lay with her.

15Then Amnon hated her with a very great hatred; the hatred with which he hated her was greater than the love with which he had loved her. Amnon said to her, "Get up, go!"

16She said to him, "No, for this wrong in sending me away is greater than the other you have done to me." But he would not listen to her.

17He called the young man who served him and said, "Put this woman out of my presence and bolt the door after her."

18She was wearing a long coat, for that is what the king's daughters who were virgins wore as robes. So his servant put her out and bolted the door after her.

19Tamar put ashes on her head and tore the long coat she was wearing. She put her hand on her head and went away, crying out as she went.

20Absalom her brother said to her, "Has Amnon your brother been with you? Now, my sister, keep quiet; he is your brother. Do not take this to heart." So Tamar lived, desolate, in her brother Absalom's house.

21When King David heard all these things, he was very angry. But he did not grieve the spirit of Amnon his son, because he loved him, for he was his firstborn.

22Absalom spoke to Amnon neither bad nor good, for Absalom hated Amnon because he had violated Tamar his sister.

Absalom's Sheep-Shearing

23And it came to pass after two full years that Absalom had sheepshearers at Baal-hazor, which is near Ephraim, and Absalom invited all the king's sons.

24Absalom came to the king and said, "Your servant has sheepshearers. Please let the king and his servants go with your servant."

25The king said to Absalom, "No, my son, let us not all go, or we will be a burden to you." He pressed him, but he would not go, and he blessed him.

26Absalom said, "If not, please let my brother Amnon go with us." The king said to him, "Why should he go with you?"

27But Absalom pressed him, and he sent Amnon and all the king's sons with him. Absalom made a feast like the feast of a king.

28Absalom commanded his young men, "Watch now. When Amnon's heart is merry with wine and I say to you, 'Strike Amnon,' then put him to death. Do not be afraid. Is it not I who have commanded you? Be strong and be men of valor."

29So Absalom's young men did to Amnon as Absalom had commanded. Then all the king's sons got up, and each mounted his mule and fled.

The News Reaches David

30And it came to pass, while they were on the way, that the report came to David: "Absalom has struck down all the king's sons, and not one of them is left."

31The king got up, tore his clothes and lay on the ground, and all his servants stood by with their clothes torn.

32But Jonadab son of Shimeah, David's brother, spoke up and said, "Let not my lord suppose that they have killed all the young men, the king's sons, for Amnon alone is dead. This has been Absalom's intent from the day Amnon violated his sister Tamar.

33So now let not my lord the king take to heart the report that all the king's sons are dead, for Amnon alone is dead."

34Absalom fled. The young man keeping watch lifted up his eyes and saw many people coming on the road behind him, by the side of the hill.

35Jonadab said to the king, "The king's sons have come. As your servant said, so it has happened."

36And it came to pass, as he finished speaking, that the king's sons came, and they lifted up their voices and wept. The king too and all his servants wept very bitterly.

37Absalom fled and went to Talmai son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. David mourned for his son every day.

38So Absalom fled and went to Geshur, and he was there three years.

39King David's heart longed to go out to Absalom, for he was comforted about Amnon, since he was dead.

  • vv12–13 "such a thing is not done in Israel. Do not do this outrage… like one of the fools" — lo ye'aseh khen be-Yisra'el… ha-nevalah ha-zot… ke-achad ha-nevalim.   • v14 "violated her" — va-ye'anneha, the word used of Shechem with Dinah, violated her (Genesis 34:2).

  • v16 "this wrong in sending me away is greater than the other" — the Hebrew begins with al odot, whose construction is uncertain; the Greek has this great wrong is greater than the other. The sense in both is that to send her away now is worse than what he has done.

  • vv18–19 "a long coat" — ketonet passim, the coat Israel made for Joseph (Genesis 37:3), and nowhere else in the Hebrew Bible. Joseph's brothers stripped it from him; Tamar tears hers.

  • v21 "But he did not grieve the spirit of Amnon his son, because he loved him, for he was his firstborn" — this sentence is in the Greek and not in the Hebrew, which ends with he was very angry.   • v27 "Absalom made a feast like the feast of a king" — also from the Greek; the Hebrew lacks it, but v28 speaks of Amnon merry with wine. The words are Nabal's feast, like the feast of a king (1 Samuel 25:36). The text follows the Greek.

  • v32 "This has been Absalom's intent" — al pi Avshalom hayetah sumah, on Absalom's mouth it was set.

  • v34 "by the side of the hill" — the Greek adds that the watchman came and told the king, I have seen men on the Horonaim road, by the side of the hill. The text stays with the Hebrew.

  • v39 "King David's heart longed to go out to Absalom" — the verb va-tekhal is feminine and has no subject: heart (or soul) is understood, as in my soul longs, even faints (Psalm 84:3). chapters.title: The Woman of Tekoa
chapters.html:
2 Samuel 14

Joab's Plan

1Joab son of Zeruiah knew that the king's heart was on Absalom.

2So Joab sent to Tekoa and brought from there a wise woman. He said to her, "Pretend to be a mourner. Put on mourning clothes and do not anoint yourself with oil, but be like a woman who has been mourning many days for the dead.

3Then go to the king and speak to him in this way." So Joab put the words in her mouth.

The Woman of Tekoa

4When the woman of Tekoa spoke to the king, she fell on her face to the ground, paid homage and said, "Save me, O king!"

5The king said to her, "What is troubling you?" She said, "I am truly a widow; my husband is dead.

6Your servant had two sons, and the two of them quarreled in the field. There was no one to part them, and one struck the other and killed him.

7Now the whole clan has risen against your servant, and they say, 'Hand over the one who struck his brother, so that we may put him to death for the life of his brother whom he killed, and destroy the heir as well.' So they would quench my coal that is left, and leave my husband neither name nor remnant on the face of the earth."

8The king said to the woman, "Go to your house, and I will give orders concerning you."

9The woman of Tekoa said to the king, "My lord the king, let the guilt be on me and on my father's house, and let the king and his throne be guiltless."

10The king said, "If anyone speaks to you, bring him to me, and he shall never touch you again."

11She said, "Please let the king remember the LORD your God, so that the avenger of blood may not destroy any more, and my son not be destroyed." He said, "As the LORD lives, not one hair of your son shall fall to the ground."

12Then the woman said, "Please let your servant speak a word to my lord the king." He said, "Speak."

13The woman said, "Why then have you planned such a thing against the people of God? In speaking this word the king is like one who is guilty, since the king does not bring back his own banished one.

14We must all die; we are like water spilled on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again. But God does not take away a life; He devises ways so that the banished one is not cast out from Him.

15Now I have come to speak this word to my lord the king because the people have made me afraid. Your servant thought, 'I will speak to the king; perhaps the king will do what his servant asks.

16For the king will hear, and deliver his servant from the hand of the man who would destroy me and my son together from the inheritance of God.'

17Your servant thought, 'Let the word of my lord the king bring rest,' for my lord the king is like the messenger of God, to discern good and evil. The LORD your God be with you!"

18Then the king answered the woman, "Do not hide from me anything I ask you." The woman said, "Let my lord the king speak."

19The king said, "Is the hand of Joab with you in all this?" The woman answered, "As your soul lives, my lord the king, no one can turn to the right or to the left from anything my lord the king has said. It was your servant Joab who commanded me; it was he who put all these words in your servant's mouth.

20Your servant Joab did this to change the face of the matter. But my lord is wise, with the wisdom of the messenger of God, to know everything that is on the earth."

21Then the king said to Joab, "I have done this thing. Go, bring back the young man Absalom."

22Joab fell on his face to the ground, paid homage and blessed the king. Joab said, "Today your servant knows that I have found favor in your eyes, my lord the king, because the king has done what your servant asked."

23So Joab got up, went to Geshur and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.

24But the king said, "Let him turn aside to his own house; he shall not see my face." So Absalom turned aside to his own house and did not see the king's face.

Absalom

25In all Israel there was no man so much to be praised for his beauty as Absalom. From the sole of his foot to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.

26When he cut the hair of his head — he cut it at the end of every year, because it was heavy on him — he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels by the king's weight.

27Three sons were born to Absalom, and one daughter whose name was Tamar. She was a beautiful woman.

28Absalom lived two full years in Jerusalem without seeing the king's face.

29Then Absalom sent for Joab, to send him to the king, but he would not come to him. He sent again a second time, but he would not come.

30So he said to his servants, "See, Joab's field is next to mine, and he has barley there. Go and set it on fire." So Absalom's servants set the field on fire.

31Then Joab got up and came to Absalom at his house and said to him, "Why have your servants set my field on fire?"

32Absalom said to Joab, "I sent word to you: 'Come here, so that I may send you to the king to say, "Why have I come from Geshur? It would be better for me if I were still there."' Now let me see the king's face, and if there is guilt in me, let him put me to death."

33So Joab went to the king and told him. He called Absalom, and he came to the king and paid homage to him with his face to the ground before the king. The king kissed Absalom.

Notes

  • v2 "a wise woman" — ishah chakhamah. Another wise woman will speak for her town at Abel (20:16). Va-yasem Yo'av et ha-devarim be-fiha, Joab put the words in her mouth (v3), the words the LORD used to Moses of Aaron, put the words in his mouth (Exodus 4:15).

  • v7 "they would quench my coal that is left" — gachalti, the one live coal kept in the ashes to light the next fire. With her last son dead, her husband's name goes out.

  • v11 "the avenger of blood" — go'el ha-dam, the kinsman whose duty was to put a killer to death (Numbers 35:19). Not one hair of your son shall fall to the ground: the king has bound himself by oath before he knows whose son it is.

  • v13 "since the king does not bring back his own banished one" — nidcho. The woman's story was a parable, as Nathan's was (12:1–7): the king has passed judgment, and the judgment applies to himself.

  • v14 "We must all die… like water spilled on the ground… God does not take away a life" — ve-lo yissa Elohim nefesh. The Greek has no negative: God will take a life. The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • v17 "Let the word of my lord the king bring rest" — li-menuchah, for rest. The Greek has for sacrifices, reading minchah, offering, for menuchah. The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • vv17, 20 "like the messenger of God, to discern good and evil… to know everything that is on the earth" — ke-mal'akh ha-Elohim. Achish said David was as good in my eyes as a messenger of God (1 Samuel 29:9).

  • v25 "there was no blemish in him" — mum, the word for a defect that bars an animal from the altar (Leviticus 22:20). Saul too was praised for his looks (1 Samuel 9:2).

  • v27 "Three sons… and one daughter whose name was Tamar" — named after his sister. Later Absalom will say I have no son to keep my name in remembrance (18:18). The Greek adds that this Tamar became the wife of Rehoboam son of Solomon and bore him Abiathar; the text stays with the Hebrew.

  • v30 "set it on fire" — the written text has ve-hotsitiha, and I will set it on fire; the text follows the read form, ve-hatsituha, set it on fire. The Greek adds that Joab's servants came to him with their clothes torn and told him. The text stays with the Hebrew.

chapters.title: Absalom's Revolt
chapters.html:
2 Samuel 15

Absalom Steals the Hearts of Israel

1And it came to pass after this that Absalom got himself a chariot and horses, and fifty men to run before him.

2Absalom would rise early and stand beside the road to the gate. Whenever any man had a dispute to bring before the king for judgment, Absalom would call to him and say, "What town are you from?" When he said, "Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel,"

3Absalom would say to him, "See, your claims are good and right, but there is no one from the king to hear you."

4Then Absalom would say, "If only I were made judge in the land! Then every man who had a dispute or a case could come to me, and I would give him justice."

5And it would come to pass, when a man came near to pay homage to him, that he would put out his hand, take hold of him and kiss him.

6Absalom did this to all Israel who came to the king for judgment. So Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.

The Conspiracy at Hebron

7And it came to pass at the end of forty years that Absalom said to the king, "Please let me go to Hebron and pay the vow I made to the LORD.

8For your servant made a vow while I lived at Geshur in Aram: 'If the LORD will indeed bring me back to Jerusalem, I will serve the LORD.'"

9The king said to him, "Go in peace." So he got up and went to Hebron.

10Then Absalom sent secret messengers throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, "As soon as you hear the sound of the shofar, say, 'Absalom has become king in Hebron!'"

11Two hundred men from Jerusalem went with Absalom. They had been invited and went in their innocence, knowing nothing of the matter.

12While he was offering the sacrifices, Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counselor, from his town, Giloh. The conspiracy grew strong, and the people with Absalom kept increasing.

David Leaves Jerusalem

13A messenger came to David and said, "The hearts of the men of Israel have gone after Absalom."

14David said to all his servants who were with him in Jerusalem, "Get up, let us flee, or none of us will escape from Absalom. Go quickly, or he will quickly overtake us, bring disaster down on us and strike the city with the sword."

15The king's servants said to the king, "Whatever my lord the king chooses, your servants are ready."

16So the king went out, and all his household after him. The king left ten women, concubines, to keep the house.

17The king went out, and all the people after him, and they stopped at the last house.

18All his servants passed on beside him, and all the Cherethites and all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men who had come after him from Gath, passed on before the king.

19Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, "Why are you also going with us? Go back and stay with the king, for you are a foreigner, and an exile from your own place as well.

20You came only yesterday; should I today make you wander about with us, when I go wherever I may go? Go back, and take your brothers with you. Loyal love and faithfulness be with you."

21But Ittai answered the king, "As the LORD lives, and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king may be, whether for death or for life, there your servant will be."

22David said to Ittai, "Go then, pass on." So Ittai the Gittite passed on, with all his men and all the little ones who were with him.

23The whole land was weeping aloud as all the people passed by. The king crossed the Kidron Valley, and all the people passed on toward the wilderness.

The Ark Sent Back

24Zadok came too, and all the Levites with him, carrying the ark of the covenant of God. They set down the ark of God, and Abiathar went up, until all the people had finished passing out of the city.

25Then the king said to Zadok, "Take the ark of God back into the city. If I find favor in the eyes of the LORD, He will bring me back and let me see both it and His dwelling.

26But if He says, 'I have no delight in you,' here I am; let Him do to me what is good in His eyes."

27The king also said to Zadok the priest, "Are you not a seer? Go back to the city in peace, and your two sons with you, Ahimaaz your son and Jonathan son of Abiathar.

28See, I will wait in the plains of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me."

29So Zadok and Abiathar took the ark of God back to Jerusalem, and they stayed there.

The Mount of Olives

30David went up the ascent of the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went, with his head covered and walking barefoot. All the people who were with him covered their heads, and they went up, weeping as they went.

31David was told, "Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom." David said, "O LORD, please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness."

32And it came to pass, as David came to the summit, where God was worshiped, that Hushai the Archite came to meet him with his coat torn and earth on his head.

33David said to him, "If you pass on with me, you will be a burden to me.

34But if you return to the city and say to Absalom, 'I will be your servant, O king; as I was your father's servant in the past, so now I will be your servant,' then you can defeat the counsel of Ahithophel for me.

35Will not Zadok and Abiathar the priests be there with you? Whatever you hear from the king's house, tell it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.

36Their two sons are there with them, Ahimaaz son of Zadok and Jonathan son of Abiathar. By them you shall send me everything you hear."

37So Hushai, David's friend, came into the city, just as Absalom was coming into Jerusalem.

Notes

  • v6 "So Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel" — va-yegannev… et lev, stole the heart, the words Jacob used when he slipped away from Laban, Jacob stole the heart of Laban (Genesis 31:20). Here it is winning loyalty by deceit.

  • v7 "at the end of forty years" — the Hebrew and the Greek both have forty. David reigned forty years in all (5:4), and this is not the end of his reign; the text does not say from what point the forty are counted.

  • v10 "secret messengers" — meraggelim, the word for spies. Absalom has become king in Hebron: Hebron is where David was first anointed king (2:4) and reigned seven years.

  • v12 "Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counselor" — his son was Eliam son of Ahithophel the Gilonite, one of David's mighty men (23:34), and Bathsheba was daughter of Eliam (11:3). The text does not say that the two Eliams are the same man.

  • vv19–21 "you are a foreigner… whether for death or for life, there your servant will be" — nokhri, a foreigner, the word Ruth used of herself (Ruth 2:10). Ittai of Gath answers as Ruth answered Naomi, Where you die, I will die (Ruth 1:17).

  • vv25–26 "He will bring me back… let Him do to me what is good in His eyes" — hineni, here I am. The words of Eli when the judgment against his house was told, Let Him do what is good in His eyes (1 Samuel 3:18).

  • v27 "Are you not a seer?" — ha-ro'eh attah, the old word for a prophet (1 Samuel 9:9). The Greek has See, reading the word as a command. The sense of the Hebrew question is uncertain.

  • v28 "in the plains of the wilderness" — the written text has be-avrot, at the fords; the read form is be-arvot, in the plains, and the text follows it. The same place is named in 17:16, where the Hebrew has be-arvot written.

  • v31 "turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness" — sakkel, from the word of Samuel to Saul, You have acted foolishly (1 Samuel 13:13). The prayer is answered in 17:14: the LORD had ordained to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel.

  • v37 "Hushai, David's friend" — re'eh David, the word of the court title re'eh ha-melekh, the king's friend, in Solomon's list of officials (1 Kings 4:5).

speech.text: 2 Samuel 15
Absalom Steals the Hearts of Israel
And it came to pass after this that Absalom got himself a chariot and horses, and fifty men to run before him.

Absalom would rise early and stand beside the road to the gate. Whenever any man had a dispute to bring before the king for judgment, Absalom would call to him and say, "What town are you from?" When he said, "Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel,"
Absalom would say to him, "See, your claims are good and right, but there is no one from the king to hear you."
Then Absalom would say, "If only I were made judge in the land! Then every man who had a dispute or a case could come to me, and I would give him justice."
And it would come to pass, when a man came near to pay homage to him, that he would put out his hand, take hold of him and kiss him.
Absalom did this to all Israel who came to the king for judgment. So Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.
The Conspiracy at Hebron
And it came to pass at the end of forty years that Absalom said to the king, "Please let me go to Hebron and pay the vow I made to the LORD.
For your servant made a vow while I lived at Geshur in Aram: 'If the LORD will indeed bring me back to Jerusalem, I will serve the LORD.'"
The king said to him, "Go in peace." So he got up and went to Hebron.
Then Absalom sent secret messengers throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, "As soon as you hear the sound of the shofar, say, 'Absalom has become king in Hebron!'"
Two hundred men from Jerusalem went with Absalom. They had been invited and went in their innocence, knowing nothing of the matter.
While he was offering the sacrifices, Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counselor, from his town, Giloh. The conspiracy grew strong, and the people with Absalom kept increasing.
David Leaves Jerusalem
A messenger came to David and said, "The hearts of the men of Israel have gone after Absalom."

David said to all his servants who were with him in Jerusalem, "Get up, let us flee, or none of us will escape from Absalom. Go quickly, or he will quickly overtake us, bring disaster down on us and strike the city with the sword."
The king's servants said to the king, "Whatever my lord the king chooses, your servants are ready."
So the king went out, and all his household after him. The king left ten women, concubines, to keep the house.
The king went out, and all the people after him, and they stopped at the last house.
All his servants passed on beside him, and all the Cherethites and all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men who had come after him from Gath, passed on before the king.
Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, "Why are you also going with us? Go back and stay with the king, for you are a foreigner, and an exile from your own place as well.
You came only yesterday; should I today make you wander about with us, when I go wherever I may go? Go back, and take your brothers with you. Loyal love and faithfulness be with you."
But Ittai answered the king, "As the LORD lives, and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king may be, whether for death or for life, there your servant will be."
David said to Ittai, "Go then, pass on." So Ittai the Gittite passed on, with all his men and all the little ones who were with him.
The whole land was weeping aloud as all the people passed by. The king crossed the Kidron Valley, and all the people passed on toward the wilderness.
The Ark Sent Back
Zadok came too, and all the Levites with him, carrying the ark of the covenant of God. They set down the ark of God, and Abiathar went up, until all the people had finished passing out of the city.
Then the king said to Zadok, "Take the ark of God back into the city. If I find favor in the eyes of the LORD, He will bring me back and let me see both it and His dwelling.
But if He says, 'I have no delight in you,' here I am; let Him do to me what is good in His eyes."
The king also said to Zadok the priest, "Are you not a seer? Go back to the city in peace, and your two sons with you, Ahimaaz your son and Jonathan son of Abiathar.
See, I will wait in the plains of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me."
So Zadok and Abiathar took the ark of God back to Jerusalem, and they stayed there.
The Mount of Olives

David went up the ascent of the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went, with his head covered and walking barefoot. All the people who were with him covered their heads, and they went up, weeping as they went.
David was told, "Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom." David said, "O LORD, please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness."
And it came to pass, as David came to the summit, where God was worshiped, that Hushai the Archite came to meet him with his coat torn and earth on his head.
David said to him, "If you pass on with me, you will be a burden to me.

But if you return to the city and say to Absalom, 'I will be your servant, O king; as I was your father's servant in the past, so now I will be your servant,' then you can defeat the counsel of Ahithophel for me.
Will not Zadok and Abiathar the priests be there with you? Whatever you hear from the king's house, tell it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
Their two sons are there with them, Ahimaaz son of Zadok and Jonathan son of Abiathar. By them you shall send me everything you hear."
So Hushai, David's friend, came into the city, just as Absalom was coming into Jerusalem.

chapters.title: Ziba and Shimei
chapters.html:
2 Samuel 16

Ziba

1When David had gone a little past the summit, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth came to meet him with a pair of saddled donkeys. On them were two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred clusters of raisins, a hundred of summer fruit and a skin of wine.

2The king said to Ziba, "What do you mean by these?" Ziba said, "The donkeys are for the king's household to ride, the bread and the summer fruit for the young men to eat, and the wine for those who grow faint in the wilderness to drink."

3The king said, "Where is your master's son?" Ziba said to the king, "He is staying in Jerusalem, for he said, 'Today the house of Israel will give me back the kingdom of my father.'"

4The king said to Ziba, "All that belonged to Mephibosheth is now yours." Ziba said, "I pay homage; let me find favor in your eyes, my lord the king."

Shimei Curses David

5When King David came to Bahurim, a man of the clan of the house of Saul came out from there. His name was Shimei son of Gera, and he came out cursing as he came.

6He threw stones at David and at all King David's servants, though all the people and all the mighty men were on his right and on his left.

7This is what Shimei said as he cursed: "Get out, get out, you man of blood, you worthless man!

8The LORD has brought back on you all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose place you have reigned, and the LORD has given the kingdom into the hand of Absalom your son. Now you are caught in your own evil, for you are a man of blood."

9Then Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king, "Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me go over and take off his head."

10But the king said, "What have I to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah? If he curses because the LORD has said to him, 'Curse David,' who then shall say, 'Why have you done so?'"

11David said to Abishai and to all his servants, "My own son, who came out of my body, seeks my life; how much more now this Benjaminite! Let him alone and let him curse, for the LORD has told him to.

12Perhaps the LORD will look on my affliction, and the LORD will repay me with good for his cursing today."

13So David and his men went on the road, while Shimei went along the side of the hill opposite him, cursing as he went, throwing stones at him and flinging dust.

14The king and all the people who were with him arrived weary, and he drew breath there.

Absalom in Jerusalem

15Meanwhile Absalom and all the people, the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him.

16And it came to pass, when Hushai the Archite, David's friend, came to Absalom, that Hushai said to Absalom, "Long live the king! Long live the king!"

17Absalom said to Hushai, "Is this your loyal love to your friend? Why did you not go with your friend?"

18Hushai said to Absalom, "No; the one whom the LORD and this people and all the men of Israel have chosen, his I will be, and with him I will stay.

19Besides, whom should I serve? Should it not be his son? As I served in your father's presence, so I will be in yours."

20Then Absalom said to Ahithophel, "Give your counsel. What shall we do?"

21Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Go in to your father's concubines, whom he left to keep the house. Then all Israel will hear that you have become a stench to your father, and the hands of all who are with you will be strengthened."

22So they pitched the tent for Absalom on the roof, and Absalom went in to his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel.

23In those days the counsel that Ahithophel gave was as if one inquired of the word of God. So was all the counsel of Ahithophel, both to David and to Absalom.

Notes

  • vv1–4 "Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth… All that belonged to Mephibosheth is now yours" — the king who gave Mephibosheth all of Saul's land (9:7–10) now gives it to Ziba on Ziba's word alone. Mephibosheth will give his own account when David returns (19:24–30).

  • v7 "you man of blood, you worthless man" — ish ha-damim ve-ish ha-beliyya'al. Beliyya'al is worthlessness, the word used of Eli's sons (1 Samuel 2:12).

  • v8 "all the blood of the house of Saul" — the deaths of Abner (3:27) and of Ish-bosheth (4:7) have been told, and the text cleared David of both: it had not been the king's will to put Abner son of Ner to death (3:37), and he executed Ish-bosheth's killers (4:9–12). Shimei's charge is his own.

  • v9 "this dead dog" — the words David used of himself before Saul (1 Samuel 24:14), and Mephibosheth before David (9:8).

  • v10 "What have I to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah?" — mah li ve-lakhem, a way of refusing someone's proposal. If he curses: the written text has ki, because, and the read form is koh, so let him curse. The text follows the read form, with little difference in sense.

  • v12 "Perhaps the LORD will look on my affliction" — the written text is be-avoni, on my guilt; the read form is be-eini, on my eye. The Greek has on my humiliation, which reads the written letters as be-onyi, on my affliction. That is the phrase of Leah, the LORD has seen my affliction (Genesis 29:32), and of Hannah, if You will indeed look on the affliction of Your servant (1 Samuel 1:11). The text follows the Greek.

  • v14 "arrived weary, and he drew breath there" — va-yinnafesh, from nefesh, breath, the word of the sabbath law, the son of your slave woman and the guest may draw breath (Exodus 23:12).

  • v17 "Is this your loyal love to your friend?" — zeh chasdekha et re'ekha. Hushai is David's friend (15:37; 16:16), and Absalom mocks the title.

  • v21 "you have become a stench to your father" — niv'ashta, the word of 10:6 and 1 Samuel 13:4. To take the king's concubines is to claim the king's place; Abner was accused over Saul's concubine (3:7).

  • v22 "they pitched the tent for Absalom on the roof… in the sight of all Israel" — David was walking on the roof of the king's house when he saw Bathsheba (11:2). Nathan had said, he shall lie with your wives before the eyes of this sun… I will do this thing before all Israel (12:11–12).
